As the season shifts, home slows with it.
Our Autumn/Winter 2026 collection celebrates the quieter pleasures of life at home. Thoughtfully crafted furniture, textiles, lighting and decorative pieces come together in a season shaped by character, craftsmanship and the beauty of everyday rituals.
From handcrafted oak furniture and rich upholstery to artisan-made ceramics, woven textiles and atmospheric lighting, each piece is designed to enrich everyday living. Together, they create homes that feel layered, welcoming and deeply personal, inviting a gentler rhythm of living.

Inspired by shifting light and weathered landscapes, this season pairs cool coastal blues with warm clay, rose and ochre tones. Layered through natural materials, tactile textiles and crafted details, the palette brings a sense of depth, warmth and quiet character to the home.
The new Ottilie Stool introduces a fresh silhouette to the collection. Compact in scale yet rich in character, its gathered skirt and piped detailing bring a playful decorative flourish.
Pairing upholstered headboards with handmade wool blankets woven in Scotland, this season's bedroom collection embraces texture, craftsmanship and the restorative comfort of slower autumn days.

As the season unfolds, thoughts begin to turn towards the rituals that gather us together. Tables prepared for long lunches, spare rooms readied for visiting guests and homes gently adapted for the months ahead. This collection lays the foundation for those moments still to come.

New for Autumn/Winter 2026, the Lewin Desk reflects an evolution of the Rowen & Wren design language. Inspired by Gustavian furniture, its reeded drawers, turned oak knobs and gently tapered legs bring together decorative detail and everyday practicality.

When designing the desk, I was drawn to the idea of it having a gentle presence. Something with a sense of structure, but softened so it felt approachable and easy to live with. It was about building on the softness and restraint that already feels familiar to Rowen & Wren, while introducing a little more refinement and detail."

ALEX BILTON, PRODUCT MANAGER

As the season unfolds, warmer tones begin to emerge. Rose velvet upholstery, weathered oak and richly patterned textiles bring depth and softness to the home, creating spaces that feel both comforting and quietly inviting.

Inspired by Gustavian furniture, the Celia Sideboard reflects this shift beautifully. Its turned detailing and softly weathered finish bring warmth, craftsmanship and enduring character to the room.

As the days grow shorter, gathering around the table takes on a new significance. Candlelight appears earlier in the evening, simple meals linger a little longer, and everyday moments become occasions to be shared.

Looking Ahead to Christmas

As autumn gently gives way to winter, the story continues with the arrival of our Christmas collection. Decorations feel gathered rather than coordinated, tables are layered overtime and familiar traditions are celebrated through thoughtful, handcrafted details.

As the days grow shorter, gathering around the table takes on a new significance. Candlelight appears earlier in the evening, simple meals linger a little longer, and everyday moments become occasions to be shared.
